name: sol_token_fe_9
description: Unrestricted flash-mint functionality enabling temporary supply inflation abuse
question: The source file in `source` implements a flash-mint function that mints an arbitrary or uncapped amount of tokens to a borrower for use within the same transaction, without enforcing that the minted tokens are burned or repaid by the end of the transaction, or without any cap/fee limiting the mintable amount, or without a reentrancy guard around the mint-callback-burn sequence, allowing the temporary supply spike to be exploited (e.g., for governance or price-oracle manipulation), excluding flash-mint logic that is restricted to a trusted admin-only caller or that already enforces repayment, caps, and reentrancy protection.
criteria: flashLoan()/flashMint() mints tokens to the receiver and calls an external callback, then checks balance only after the call without verifying the exact minted amount was burned or returned
flashMint() has no maximum-amount cap, allowing the caller to mint an amount large enough to manipulate a price or voting-power snapshot within the same transaction
flashMint() executes the external callback and burn/repayment logic without a reentrancy guard, allowing reentrant calls to mint additional tokens before the original mint is settled
flashMint() burns only a previously recorded balance rather than re-checking totalSupply post-callback, allowing the borrower to keep part of the minted tokens uncollected
